title: RAW UNREVIEWED: paired X-daiin fields record separate completion of two linked postings
summary: RAW_UNREVIEWED. Start from GDT877's real pchedal-qopchdy-daiin anchor and GDT764's adjacent chedy-daiin field, not a presumed numeral. In the complete f105v.5–7 paragraph, explore one context-bound POSTED predicate over two account roles. Pacioli's owned precious-stones example marks debit and credit separately, preserves their common transaction and value, then records opposed account references. One completed side does not complete the other; two equal scalar values alone do not establish this dependency.

design.mechanism: A record binds a shared transaction; repeated FIELD(X,POSTED) constructions update separate posting obligations. The two account roles are distinct while the transaction/date/value remain shared, and later counterreferences must resolve the opposite role.
design.unit: Complete already admitted f105v.5–7,30 literal groups in each reader. ZL and IT independently supply the same paragraph-start/end flags; RF is the complete corresponding spatial union, not an independently flagged paragraph. The exact source projection is retained as L_F105V_COMPLETE_PARAGRAPH.tsv.
design.contrast: Two coupled completion flags versus two independent quantities/grades in a nominal list, or one global DONE flag that prematurely closes the transaction after its first completed entry.
design.prediction: After the first field is marked, one posting remains due; after both, the posting pair is complete but its references must still name the correct opposed accounts. A wrong counteraccount can preserve equality of amounts while violating the reading. Replacing the repeated flag by one common amount does not produce either the pending-obligation state or the reciprocal ownership constraint.
actual_positive_referents: GDT877 verifies pchedal qopchdy daiin at f105v.5 as three consecutive literal groups with definite internal gaps in all three readers. GDT764 retains the same complete opening as pchedal | qopchdy daiin | chedy daiin | ..., and withdraws an unsupported imperative for qopchdy at this location.

The selected complete paragraph contains the two fields in .5 and the later literal sequence dar aiin al dar ar in .6, in all three readings. That later sequence is a possible pair of reference-bearing expressions, not a discovered counterreference or a reading of dar.

GDT318's global entry-context effect supplies a real precedent for context-sensitive rendering, but no particular wrapper, transaction, nominal class or completion meaning. No part of pchedal is translated here.

IDEA400's complete owned Pacioli1494 teaching item gives stones debit on page3, capital credit on page2, a shared40/0/0/0 amount/date, two separate Journal marking acts, opposed page references and subsequent indexing. The source's informational identity is not physical transport or stock conservation.
additional_assumptions: Within this explicitly nominated paired-field construction, daiin tentatively contributes POSTED rather than valueIII. This is one contextual semantic hypothesis; no universal daiin meaning is installed.
qopchdy and chedy are the two distinct account-role parameters A and B. Their actual names remain unknown; no stones/capital translations or character decomposition are assigned.
The initial H1 record supplies a transaction frame with two obligations. This binder is a proposed construction, not a semantic result of the existing H1 position statistics.

A later part of the complete paragraph must bind both account references and their shared transaction. The observed dar...dar string merely nominates where to attempt this; it does not supply its own arguments or permit an arbitrary silent address map.

finite_core.frame: T = (accountA, accountB, shared_value, shared_date, postedA=false, postedB=false).
finite_core.field_rule: X daiin -> POSTED(T,X) for an explicitly bound account role X. The same predicate applies to both fields.
finite_core.sequence: The first field changes only postedA; the second changes only postedB. Transaction-posting completion requires both. This is not a claim that every chronological act in Pacioli is encoded in these five groups.
finite_core.reference_constraint: A's counterreference resolves to B and B's to A, preserving the same T. The account-name/address map must be written or supplied by one explicit local binding rule before any success is claimed.
finite_core.not_imported: No40,3,2,November8,precious-stone name, debit glyph, credit glyph, s/q/d prefix translation, numeric additive code or old HOT/COLD value is mapped into the target.
finite_core.unknowns: Only two daiin positions receive a conditional contextual predicate; qopchdy and chedy are typed variables, not lexical identifications. The transaction binder, counterreferences, date/value and remaining26 positions are not translated. The whole30-position unit remains present.
finite_core.scope: The historical source is a full teaching item with layout, indexing and explanatory prose. This candidate borrows its linked-posting mechanism; it does not claim that the30 target groups translate that entire pedagogical item. A complete target reading still owes every target group and any chosen content beyond the core.

design.strongest_known_countercase: GDT764's value-field analysis already competes with this flag reading, and GDT877 validates only literal form/gaps. No target transaction or account is identified. Other saved daiin uses include the adjacent daiin-daiin on f32v.8; a later portable rule cannot pretend that these automatically name two different postings. W94/W95 show why repeated forms do not establish a common physical quantity, and analogous care is required for this proposed common transaction. RF lacks paragraph flags, and several literal groups in .5–7 remain reader-dependent.
design.smallest_next_step: A single local authoring pass: preserve all30 groups, write the two FIELD scopes and their shared frame, then attempt a concrete counterreference account for all of .6–7 using at most one additional reference construction and no new named commodities. Compare the four posting-status states and both account orientations by hand. If only two unconstrained X slots and two completion labels can be written, the result is a partial hypothesis, not a bookkeeping reading. Do not start a global daiin census or numeric decoder.
design.novelty_and_dependencies: IDEA400 owns the Pacioli source and generic reciprocal-reference mechanism. This card is a dependent application with an exact three-line target and a different local semantic rival: repeated completion status versus repeated numerical value. It does not claim to discover paired fields, ledger balancing, or that empty posted searches establish novelty. IDEA14's overt-single-material contract, the f22r apposition cards and GDT1040's fixed loan grammar are not reused or reopened.
design.source_layer: Pacioli1494 is after1450. The owned complete local reading is Geijsbeek1914 English translation, with partial Italian-facsimile checks and recorded conflicts. It demonstrates a historical nonbotanical writing mechanism, not an early15th-century source identification.
design.claim_ceiling: RAW_UNREVIEWED. One small context-bound meaning hypothesis, not a complete ledger reading, confirmed numeral, portable predicate or independently scored relation. No image, source hunt, reserve or contact.
